searchText: yes, thank you for clarifying on this. i read through the article once more and realized the parallel i thought of is likely not applicable. from my understanding the expiration of a state object according to the time-to-life value is a linear progress. as a consequence it's either inactive or active if touched/witnessed in the meantime. how long would that time-to-life value likely endure? I think roughly 1 year is the usual answer? <dankrad> https://dankradfeist.de/ethereum/2021/02/14/why-stateless.html Worth noting, Polkadot seems to be using a similar idea of resource-heavy block producers/collators, who do not participate in consensus https://wiki.polkadot.network/docs/en/learn-collator <dankrad> I think it's the logical conclusion, if you want decentralisation and performance
